title: Allow linking a non-nested abbreviation to its definition

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

For terms that have an abbreviation, two common patterns to define them (see e.g., [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/abbr#defining_an_abbreviation)) are:

```html
<dfn><abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr></dfn>
```

and 

```html
<dfn>HyperText Markup Language</dfn> (<abbr>HTML</abbr>)
```

With the former pattern, the link between the `dfn` and `abbr` elements is encoded in the nesting of the elements.
With the latter pattern, there is no link between the `abbr` element and the `dfn` element.

### What solutions exist today?

1. define a custom element:

```html
<foo-abbr-dfn abbr="HTML">HyperText Markup Language</foo-abbr-dfn>
```

2. define a `data-*` attribute:

```html
<dfn id="dfn-html">HyperText Markup Language</dfn> (<abbr data-for="dfn-html">HTML</abbr>)
```

3. ... (I bet there's additional solutions I haven't thought of)

### How would you solve it?

* by adding an `abbr` attribute to dfn, where `<dfn abbr="HTML">HyperText Markup Language</dfn>` would be specified to render as `HyperText Markup Language (HTML)`
* by adding a `for` attribute to the `abbr` element, analogous to the `label` element

The first solution results in succinct markup and has a nice symmetry with

 ```html
<abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>
```

(For maximum symmetry, a `dfn` attribute would have to be introduced on the `abbr` element as well, where:

```html
<abbr dfn="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>
```

would be specified to be equivalent to:

```html
<dfn><abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr></dfn>
```
)

### Anything else?

_No response_
